narration.full_text: Namaste students! Ready to test your understanding of Arithmetic Progressions? Let's dive into some questions to solidify your knowledge. First question: In which situation does the list of numbers involved make an arithmetic progression? The taxi fare after each km when the fare is Rs15 for the first km and Rs8 for each additional km. Is this an AP? Yes, it forms an AP because the common difference is constant, which is 8. The sequence is 15, 23, 31, and so on. Next, consider the amount of air present in a cylinder when a vacuum removes 1/4 of the air remaining in the cylinder at a time. Does this form an AP? No, it does not form an AP. The difference between consecutive terms is not constant, as it's a geometric progression. Moving on, the cost of digging a well after every metre of digging, when it costs Rs150 for the first metre and rises by Rs50 for each subsequent metre. Does this make an AP? Yes, this forms an AP because the common difference is constant, which is 50. The sequence is 150, 200, 250, and so on. Now, the amount of money in an account every year, when Rs 10000 is deposited at compound interest at 8% per annum. Is this an AP? No, it does not form an AP. The difference between consecutive terms is not constant due to compound interest. Let's try writing the first four terms of an AP when a = 10 and d = 10. The terms are 10, 20, 30, 40. For the AP: 3, 1, -1, -3..., what are the first term and the common difference? The first term 'a' is 3, and the common difference 'd' is -2. Which of the following is an AP? 2, 4, 8, 16... If it is, find 'd' and three more terms. This does not form an AP because the differences are 2, 4, 8, which are not constant. Finally, fill in the blank: If a=7, d=3, n=8, then an=?. The 8th term, a_n, is 28. Great job, everyone! Keep practicing!

visual_beats.description: Title: Test Your Knowledge: Arithmetic Progressions (Part 1)

Q: In which of the following situations, does the list of numbers involved make an arithmetic progression, and why? 1. The taxi fare after each km when the fare is Rs15 for the first km and Rs8 for each additional km
A: Yes, it forms an AP because the common difference is constant (8). The sequence is 15, 23, 31, ...

Q: In which of the following situations, does the list of numbers involved make an arithmetic progression, and why? 2. The amount of air present in a cylinder when a vacuum removes 1/4 of the air remaining in the cylinder at a time.
A: No, it does not form an AP because the difference between consecutive terms is not constant. The sequence is V, 3V/4, 9V/16, ... which is a geometric progression.

Q: In which of the following situations, does the list of numbers involved make an arithmetic progression, and why? iii). The cost digging a well after every metre of digging, when it costs Rs150 for the first metre and rises by Rs50 for each subsequent metre.
A: Yes, it forms an AP because the common difference is constant (50). The sequence is 150, 200, 250, ...

Q: In which of the following situations, does the list of numbers involved make an arithmetic progression, and why? iv). The amount of money in the account every year, when Rs 10000 is deposited at compound interest at 8% per annum.

A: No, it does not form an AP because the difference between consecutive terms is not constant. The amounts are 10800, 11664, ... and the differences are 800, 864, ... Q: Write first four terms of the AP, when the first term 'a' and the common difference 'd' are given as follows: (i) a = 10, d = 10 A: 10, 20, 30, 40

Q: For the following APs, write the first term and the common difference: i) 3, 1, -1, -3... A: First term a = 3, common difference d = -2. Q: Which of the following are APs? If they form an AP, find the common difference 'd' and write three more terms: i) 2, 4, 8, 16... A: Does not form an AP.
